feed.title: A readable public mirror of this list’s archive

entry.title: A readable public mirror of this list’s archive
entry.summary:
A new public archive for the Bitcoin Development Mailing List has been established at [https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive). This archive is a daily-refreshed clone, sourced from the public-inbox hosted at gnusha.org through 0xB10C’s mirror. The structure presents each discussion thread as a separate page, organized chronologically. Quoted text within messages is collapsed to simplify reading, and extraneous footers are omitted. Each individual message includes a direct link to its original location on gnusha.org, along with a unique permalink formatted by Message-ID for easy reference.
The archive offers three main indexes built atop the mirrored data. First, curated topic timelines provide an organized overview of ongoing discussions. Second, dedicated pages exist for each BIP (Bitcoin Improvement Proposal) that has been discussed within the list, allowing for focused exploration of specific technical enhancements. Third, author-specific pages are generated for individuals who have contributed ten or more messages, streamlining access to their body of work. Messages themselves are preserved in their original form, with only a brief introductory paragraph added to each topic page for context. Author identity management is implemented by merging all variants of email addresses used by the same contributor into a single author page; corrections or privacy requests can be accommodated upon notification.
Thread organization relies primarily on References headers to maintain accurate conversation threading, with subject matching used as a fallback for older replies lacking proper headers. Users are encouraged to report any mis-threaded conversations for correction. Although this new archive provides enhanced accessibility and browsing features, gnusha.org continues to serve as the canonical archive of record for the mailing list. Suggestions for inclusion in the master list of archives at [https://gnusha.org/url/](https://gnusha.org/url/) are welcomed, ensuring comprehensive documentation of available resources.
